subject: Subprocessor gating and export assurance for pilot deployment
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@evensonhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Evenson Health Procurement <procurement@evensonhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on subprocessor gating and export assurance for pilot

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed. Before procurement signs off on a short pilot (SOW to follow), legal has a couple of narrow asks we need addressed in the DPA and onboarding materials:

1) Subprocessor gating: we require a gating step where Evenson can approve or reject any new subprocessor that will process customer-provided data. Please confirm whether Redwood supports a manual approval workflow or, alternatively, an automated allowlist per account.

2) No-training / model-improvement opt-out: we need an explicit commitment in the DPA for no model training on our interaction data, plus operational evidence showing how requests marked as "no-train" are segregated.

3) Export assurance & cross-border controls: because some records may reference EU nationals, we need confirmation of where logs and backups are stored and a brief export plan (SFTP/air-gapped export options) if we request export of tenant data.

Could you share a short attestation (one page) + the current subprocessor inventory and a proposed timeline to get this live? Procurement wants to know whether these are deal-breakers before running the redline.

Appreciate it —
Maria Garcia
Director, Vendor Risk Management
Evenson Health

[Attachment: example_dpa_clauses.pdf (pdf)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@evensonhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on subprocessor gating and export assurance for pilot

Maria — thanks for the clear list. Quick response and proposed next steps below.

On Sun, Aug 15, 2026 at 09:12 AM Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@evensonhealth.com> wrote:
> Hannah,
>
> Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed. Before procurement signs off...

Summary & next steps we can commit to immediately:
- Subprocessor gating: We can offer an account-level allowlist + a manual notification window. Operationally we can flag new subprocessor requests and hold them for a 5-business-day approval by the account owner; if Evenson requires manual sign-off we can enable that for the pilot.
- No-training opt-out: Redwood supports tenant-level no-training flags. We will provide an "attestation" describing how requests are routed to non-learning execution pools and how KV/prefix caching is segregated.
- Export assurance: We will provide the subprocessor inventory, a short export runbook (SFTP + API export options), and an explanation of where backups/logs reside and cross-border safeguards.

Proposed timeline:
1) Today — share initial draft 1-page attestation + subprocessor inventory (we'll attach to this thread).
2) 8/16 — legal redline from Evenson; internal review and operational feasibility check (Kimberly, can you confirm the manual approval flow and 5-business-day window?)
3) 8/17 — final attestation + DocuSign link if redline is accepted.

I'll attach a starter attestation and the inventory in my next email. If Procurement prefers a different cadence let me know.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: starter_attestation_onepager.docx (docx)]

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on subprocessor gating and export assurance for pilot

Hannah / Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick plan. A few legal notes to make the attestation procurement-ready:

- Attestation content: include a short description of the technical separation for the no-training path (runtime flag, isolated model variant or deployment pool, confirmation that we do not persist candidate training datasets). Avoid product-internal names; keep it customer-facing.

- Subprocessor inventory: provide names, role (e.g., monitoring, logging, cloud infra), and whether they have access to decrypted customer content. We can mark sensitive entries proprietary but procurement will expect at minimum a clear indication of who can access cleartext.

- Export assurance: include contact runbook steps and SLAs for export requests (48 hours for data extract, encrypted SFTP with on-prem public key exchange). Also state default storage regions for logs/backups and whether backups include tenant PII.

Kimberly — please confirm operationally that: 
1) We can enable an account-level manual approval gate for new subprocessors for pilot customers.
2) The 5-business-day hold window is operationally feasible.
3) We can produce a CSV inventory with columns: subprocessor, role, access_type, country, contract_reference.

If yes, I'll draft redline suggestions for the DPA (no-training clause + attestation appendix) and attach them so Hannah can send to Evenson.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Legal — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

> On Aug 15, 2026, at 11:03 AM, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> > I'll attach a starter attestation and the inventory in my next email.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on subprocessor gating and export assurance for pilot

All —

Confirmed operationally: we can enable a per-account manual gating flag. Implementation notes:
- New-subprocessor flow: when a new subprocessor is onboarded and assigned to a customer-facing workflow, it will be flagged and an automated notification is sent to the account owner. We can flip to "manual approval required" for Evenson.
- 5-business-day window: OK for pilot. If no response, default will be "rejected" until manual approval is received (this is conservative but aligns with their ask).
- Inventory CSV: we can produce the columns David requested; sensitivity: for infra providers we will mark "no access to cleartext" where applicable, and for subcontractors that can access decrypted content we will provide contract refs.

I'll attach the CSV and a redline of the attestation language for review.

Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
